title: 3D Quantification of Vascular-Like Structures in z Stack Confocal Images
protocol: Start Amira and open the converted tiff file.
Import the tiff file into Amira and provide the voxel size.
Attach the Correct Z Drop module by right-clicking on the input data.
Adjust the settings in the properties window.
A new corrected object is created.
Click on the Wrapper: Image Filters module to open the Preference view and adjust the settings.
Select the [filename].corrected object as the Data Source.
Filter: Smoothing: Median; 3D.
Set the Kernel size to 3 for a 3 × 3 × 3 pixel mask in 3D.
Click on “Apply” to create the filtered object in the Project View.
Repeat step to create a second Wrapper: Image Filters module for Gaussian blur.
Select the [filename]-filtered object as the Data Source.
Filter: Smoothing: Gaussian; 3D.
Set the Kernel size to 3 × 3 × 3.
Set the Sigma Rel to 1 in x, y, and z.
Observe the outcome to ensure all key objects are visible without artifacts.
Attach the Deconvolution module in Amira.
Adjust settings in the Properties view for the deconvolution algorithm.
Set a border width of 0 in x, 0 in y, and 75 in z with 20 iterations to reduce boundary artifacts.
Choose constant initial estimate, fixed overrelaxation, no intensity-based regularization, and standard (non-blind) deconvolution method.
Derive point spread function parameters from the numerical aperture of the objective (NA, 0.45), wavelength of transmitted light (π, 0.52), and refractive index of specimen (n, 1.333).
Set mode to confocal in Amira.
Export [filename].deconv file as a tiff file after applying deconvolution algorithm.
Adjust settings based on relevance for your image or use the extract point spread function from an imaged bead.
Export the deconvoluted image by clicking on the [filename].deconv object in the Project view and choose “File” -> “Export Data As.”
Change the file type to “3D Tiff (∗.tif).”
Open the deconvoluted tiff image in Fiji (Figure 5[href=https://www.wicell.org#fig5]A).
Binarize the image in Fiji using the Otsu method.
Tick the “Stack” option to process all slices of one stack.
Open the deconvoluted images in Fiji or Amira.
Open the Auto Threshold module within the image processing software.
Set the properties for thresholding, including method and background color options.
Apply the auto-threshold settings to generate a binarized (black and white) image.
Save the binarized image as a TIFF file.
Use “Image” -> “Stacks” -> “Z Project” in Fiji or equivalent function in Amira to visualize the thresholding outcome on a 2D projection.
Open the binarized image in Amira.
Attach the Multi-Thresholding module by right-clicking on the binarized input object.
Adjust settings in the Preference view of the Multi-Thresholding module to label black (0) pixels as exterior.
Set the Exterior-Inside value to 0.
Click “Apply” to create a [filename].labels object.
Switch to the Segmentation view.
Select the binarized input image as Image source and the [filename].labels object as Label field.
Check the box at Inside 3D to view a 3D model of the data.
Go to “Segmentation” -> “Remove Islands.”
Select the appropriate settings for removing small particles.
Select a size filter in voxel from the dialog box.
Use the pictogram to explain the neighbor merging function.
Preview islands using the “Highlight all islands” button.
Click “Apply” and close the dialog box when finished.
Switch back to the Projects view.
Right-click on the [filename].labels object and attach a Chamfer Distance map module.
Open the Preference view by clicking on the Chamfer Distance Map module.
Adjust settings in the Preference view.
Use a Chamfer Distance Map module to create a distance map.
Set the interpretation to XY planes.
Select the labels object and right click to attach a Thinner module by searching or navigating through "Image Processing" -> "Skeletonization" -> "Thinner".
Open the Preference view of the Thinner module.
Select the [filename].labels object as data source.
Select the [filename].distmap object as Distmap source.
Set the len of ends parameter according to your dataset and structures of interest, using a size of 5 voxel for sample data.
Click on “Apply” to create a [filename].thinned object.
Convert the thinned image into a Spatial Graph object.
Use the Trace Lines module for conversion.
Adjust settings in the Preference view of the Trace Lines module.
Create a [filename].Spatial-Graph object after applying settings.
Attach a Smooth Line Set module to the [filename].Spatial-Graph object.
Smooth the spatial graph using the Smooth Line Set module.
